source_message.text: In that case, we can supply it from 5v and include a level shifter, unless there is a led that supports 3.3 power and logic.

source_message.text: Wouldn't the 5V_EN pin address this? When the LEDs are unnecessary, GPIO3 can shut off the complete 5V rail and reduce standby current to zero.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Since the SK6812 has a minimum supply voltage of 3.5–3.7V, a 3.3V supply is below specification and the LED may not illuminate reliably. It should be powered from 5V, with the 74AHCT1G125 level shifter (LCSC C151417) used on the data line. At 5V, the data threshold is 3.5V, which exceeds the ESP32 output level. This is already part of the design, so no other changes are required; simply replace the IRLML2402 with the 74AHCT1G125.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Perfect. Regarding the leds, I think a level shifter is necessary. Also, the LED board doc specifies C2890036 (SK6812 Mini-E, 3228 package), whereas you shared C5142047 (SK6812SMINI-ER, 2835 package). Which one exactly do you intend to use so that I can revise the documents?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs now use 3.3V power rather than 5V. With a 3.3V supply, the SK6812 data threshold decreases to 2.31V, and the ESP32 3.3V output meets it directly, eliminating the need for a level shifter. The downside is that 3.3V is somewhat below the SK6812 datasheet minimum of 3.7V, although it operates reliably at indicator brightness levels.

value_updates.accepted_operating_condition: Reliable at indicator brightness levels despite operating below the 3.7V datasheet minimum
